core_obligations: Reduce to functors (proof lines 3629-3632): points of the site correspond to points of the associated topos, so it suffices to prove the first part.

Record the properties of a point (proof lines 3633-3645): the functor preserves the final object, fibre products and coverings, sends open subschemes to subsets, is the stalk of the representable sheaf, and turns disjoint unions into disjoint unions.

Construct the comparison map (proof lines 3717-3782): for an affine object and a geometric point, the author chooses an auxiliary affine object over which the base change splits into components, uses a section to define the value of the map, and verifies that the construction is independent of the choices.

Conclude (proof lines 3784-3789): the map is functorial in the object by the same kind of argument, and bijectivity follows from the earlier paragraph, which finishes the proof of the first part and hence of the lemma.
proof_roadmap: Reduce points of the site to points of the topos and record the categorical properties of a point.
Construct a bijection between the points of an affine object over a geometric point and the values of the given point, using a splitting after base change.
Verify well-definedness, functoriality and bijectivity, and conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that points of the small etale site of a scheme, and points of its topos, are exactly those induced by geometric points (statement lines 3609-3626). The proof is a long construction: the categorical properties of a point are recorded (proof lines 3633-3645); a comparison map is built for affine objects by splitting a base change into components and using a section, and its independence of the choices is verified (proof lines 3717-3782); and functoriality together with bijectivity completes the argument (proof lines 3784-3789). The non-formal content is the construction of the comparison map and the verification that it does not depend on the auxiliary choices. The claim is H2: a construction carried out in several stages with every input named.
